plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 to address the '120 nm backbone' artifact observed in prior iterations where multiple layers converged to the 120 nm upper bound. Four complementary routes proposed: (1) reinitialize pinned layers with broader 30-150 nm window and simulated annealing, (2) increase layer count to 28 for additional degrees of freedom, (3) seed from UV-centered quarter-wave stack then optimize, (4) explore asymmetric HfO2/SiO2 thickness ratios. All routes maintain 200-400 nm UV rejection and 800-1500 nm SWIR transmission objectives with HfO2/SiO2 on fused silica substrate.

routes.title: Disrupted Initialization with Simulated Annealing to Break 120 nm Clustering
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The 120 nm thickness clustering in prior iterations represents a local minimum artifact from bound-constrained gradient descent. Randomly reinitializing layers previously pinned at 120 nm within a 30-150 nm window, followed by simulated annealing optimization, will escape this local minimum and achieve higher dual-band performance.
routes.design_principle: Disrupt symmetric thickness clustering by random reinitialization of bound-saturated layers, then use simulated annealing's temperature-dependent acceptance probability to explore broader thickness space before converging.
routes.proposed_topology: 24 alternating layers starting with HfO2 on substrate, ending with SiO2 at air interface. Exact sequence: Substrate | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Air
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
Maintain robustness under ±15 nm thickness tolerance
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds 30-150 nm compatible with standard deposition control
HfO2/SiO2 material pair well-established for space optics
theory_basis: Needle optimization technique for non-quarter-wave designs (evidence: CorpusId:225461372)
Evolutionary optimization with selection/mutation/crossover operations (evidence: CorpusId:243942968)
HfO2/SiO2 heterostructure refractive index contrast enables interference filtering (evidence: CorpusId:254823355)
expected_advantages: Breaks local minimum trapping from prior gradient-only optimization
Simulated annealing explores broader solution space
Maintains proven 24-layer topology while improving thickness distribution
known_risks: Simulated annealing may require more iterations to converge
Random initialization may temporarily reduce target score before improvement
No guarantee of finding global optimum
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2/SiO2 repeated 12 times (24 total finite layers). Initialize all layer thicknesses uniformly random within 30-150 nm range. Use simulated annealing optimizer with initial temperature 0.1, cooling rate 0.95, minimum temperature 0.001. Optimize thicknesses to maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band and mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Apply ±15 nm absolute normal thickness tolerance for robustness evaluation. Total layer count fixed at 24. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 200-400 nm, 800-1500 nm. soft objectives: High transmission in 800-1500 nm band; High reflection in 200-400 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low transmission in 200-400 nm band; Low reflection in 800-1500 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layers <= 30; Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Directly addresses feedback directive to disrupt the '120 nm backbone' artifact by reinitializing all layers within broader 30-150 nm window and switching from gradient descent to simulated annealing to escape local minima.

routes.title: Increased Layer Count (28 Layers) for Additional Design Freedom
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The 24-layer topology constrains the achievable dual-band performance. Increasing to 28 layers (still within 30-layer limit) provides additional degrees of freedom for the optimizer to shape the spectral response, potentially achieving higher UV rejection without compromising SWIR transmission.
routes.design_principle: More layers enable finer spectral shaping through additional interference conditions. The 4 extra layers allow better transition between UV stopband and SWIR passband.
routes.proposed_topology: 28 alternating layers starting with HfO2 on substrate, ending with SiO2 at air interface. Exact sequence: Substrate | (HfO2 | SiO2) × 14 | Air. Total finite layer count = 28.

Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
Maintain robustness under ±15 nm thickness tolerance
manufacturing_considerations: 4 additional layers increase deposition time but remain feasible

routes.title: UV Quarter-Wave Seeded Optimization with Transition Zone Focus
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing from a quarter-wave stack designed for UV center wavelength (300 nm) provides a physically meaningful starting point that already achieves high UV reflectance. Subsequent optimization can then improve SWIR transmission while maintaining UV rejection, avoiding the local minimum trap of arbitrary initialization.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks at UV wavelength provide high UV reflectance by construction. Starting from this baseline and optimizing allows the algorithm to modify thicknesses primarily to improve SWIR transmission rather than discovering UV reflectance from scratch.
routes.proposed_topology: 24 alternating layers starting with HfO2 on substrate, ending with SiO2 at air interface. Exact sequence: Substrate | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Air. Initial thicknesses: HfO2 = 37 nm (QW at 300 nm), SiO2 = 52 nm (QW at 300 nm).
design_variables: All 24 layer thicknesses (30-150 nm bounds, seeded from QW values)

routes.title: Asymmetric HfO2/SiO2 Thickness Ratio Exploration
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The symmetric thickness bounds (30-150 nm for both materials) may not reflect optimal optical path length ratios. HfO2 (n≈2.0) and SiO2 (n≈1.45) have different refractive indices, so optimal physical thicknesses should differ. Allowing asymmetric bounds (HfO2: 25-100 nm, SiO2: 35-150 nm) better matches optical thickness equivalence and may improve dual-band performance.
routes.design_principle: Optical thickness (n×d) determines interference conditions. For equal optical thickness, HfO2 requires ~72% of SiO2 physical thickness due to higher refractive index. Asymmetric bounds reflect this physical reality.
routes.proposed_topology: 24 alternating layers starting with HfO2 on substrate, ending with SiO2 at air interface. Exact sequence: Substrate | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Air. Total finite layer count = 24.

manufacturing_considerations: Asymmetric bounds reflect material-specific deposition characteristics
